purpose: Narrow engineering interface/source-priority/model comparison; no formal trial or runtime certification
model_comparison_limits: 6.1-sol cannot use effort none; temperature omitted, effort low. Equal one-call and 10000 input/2500 total completion-token caps are not equal visible-output or reasoning compute. Report truncation, latency and all usage including reasoning. Public 6-series IDs have no dated snapshot in current official docs; preserve returned model and fingerprint, no substitutions.

availability_preflight.method: read-only models.retrieve, no task or generation

system_prompt: Decide whether one static public/private partition can faithfully describe ALL modeled decision times in the supplied rules. Return JSON in the supplied proposal schema. Choose decision=candidate with 1 to 3 distinct partitions and witness=null when representable. Choose decision=refusal with candidates=[] and a true visibility-change witness when the SAME field changes visibility for a player over modeled times; never force a static fit or split/rename fields. Assign every field exactly once in each candidate. A witness has field, integer player 0 or 1, boolean before_visible and after_visible. left_fields/right_fields in feedback are counterfactual worlds at the SAME modeled time, NOT temporal transitions. observed_same compares that player's legal observations, not whether all state fields equal. Output only the proposal; a deterministic serializer owns envelope constants and identifiers. Never invent evidence, reliability, prior, posterior or certification.
source_priority_prompt: Source priority: RULES are authoritative about the game. A preceding assistant message is only a FALLIBLE CANDIDATE PROPOSAL to inspect or replace; it is not a new rule, observation or trusted evidence. STRUCTURE_OK means syntactic/field-structure validity only, NEVER semantic correctness. Feedback witnesses are evaluator-owned counterexamples for testing candidates, not changes to the rules. A candidate conflicting with rules or witnesses should be replaced; that conflict alone does NOT make the game out of schema. Determine temporal visibility solely from RULES. This policy does not tell you whether this particular rule is representable.

output_contract.intermediate: decision, candidates, witness only; all keys required; candidate IDs, game_id, schema_version, status and error_code are generated by deterministic serializer, never copied from model output
output_contract.schema_factor: Both modes receive identical JSON schema in prompt. f0 requests JSON object; f1 additionally uses API strict json_schema. Same semantic cross-field and independent evaluation checks in both.
output_contract.serializer_limits: does not select decision, owner or witness; refuses extra keys, mixed branches, bool/float player, out-of-vocabulary fields or malformed proposals; never normalizes old v3 replies
output_contract.historical_interpretation: New intermediate representation in ALL v4 cells; cannot attribute v3-v4 differences to schema constraint alone or retrospectively pass v3 lowercase failures

schedule.order: scope eight original v3 rules, repair four original static rules, then four frozen sealed-bid surface probes; case/repeat/rotating arm order; separate same plan per model
schedule.provider_failure: stop that model, retain assigned denominators and incomplete trials; other preregistered models may run; never substitute or repair provider parameters after a task error
schedule.token_preflight: common conservative UTF-8 byte bound plus original chat overhead; authoritative usage caps remain unchanged

sealed_bid_probes.interpretation: Frozen before v4 calls, not new game families or confirmatory holdouts. Designed after inspecting v3 failure, so cannot prove absence of selection overfitting.

renamed.method: mechanically rename field in original p3 rules, meanings, owner mapping and evidence, no ownership/timing change

phase_wording.static_rules: At every modeled decision time t, both players observe prize. Player 0 observes commitment and never observes hand. Player 1 observes hand and never observes commitment. This is true at t=0 and t=1. No disclosure occurs during these modeled decisions.
phase_wording.dynamic_rules: At modeled time t=0, both players observe prize, player 0 observes commitment, and player 1 observes hand but cannot observe commitment. At modeled time t=1, both players observe the SAME commitment as well as prize. At both times hand is observed only by player 1. A single model must cover BOTH t=0 and t=1 without changing, splitting or renaming any field.

evaluation.primary: per original pair joint correct static candidate and strict dynamic refusal; reference verified after one fixed witness-repair reply; every cell and every model reported
evaluation.probes: report original p3, field-renamed p3, phase-worded p3 separately and do not pool as independent games
evaluation.comparisons: strict vs free intermediate schema within source setting; source-priority vs no-priority within format; all three models on identical plan. No selection of only best cell.
evaluation.uncertainty: four reused primary pairs, technical repeats and two dependent surface probes; no population CI, significance or formal power claim
evaluation.independent: reuse unchanged v3 final-score evaluator, including predeclared alternative valid p2 witness; no training regret or self-certificate
evaluation.resource: report conservative uncached token cost, actual usage/reasoning details and latency independently; anomaly caps do not establish effectiveness
